party.6.why: Whether functional (occupational) representation through unions and guilds should replace party competition. Syndicalist, guild-socialist, Hegelian, corporatist and functional-group regimes say yes; liberals, libertarians, social democrats and party-state communists keep parties or individual representation; Jacobins and Objectivists reject corporate bodies outright.

notes.GS: G.D.H. Cole, Guild Socialism Restated (1920): functional democracy, with representation by occupational guilds rather than territorial parties: 3.
notes.SU: Sukarno's 1957 'bury the parties' speech and Guided Democracy replaced party rule with an appointed National Council of functional groups (golongan fungsional): 3.
notes.NATC: Salazar's 1933 Constitution and Franco's 'organic democracy' (family, municipality, syndicate) set up corporative chambers in place of party politics: 3.
notes.JA: The Le Chapelier law (1791), upheld by the Republic, abolished guilds and all intermediate bodies between citizen and nation: -3.
notes.OB: Rand rejects collectivist group representation as tribalism; only the individual has rights: -3.
notes.TAR: Poujade's UDCA (1953) organised shopkeepers and artisans as a trade body against 'the parties' in Paris: 2.
notes.GAU: De Gaulle's failed 1969 referendum would have merged the Senate with the Economic and Social Council to give occupational representation, and he denounced the 'régime des partis': 2.
notes.NA: Nasser's Arab Socialist Union reserved half of all seats for workers and peasants and grouped the 'working forces' by class and function: 2, split because it was a single party.
notes.IB: Hassan al-Banna argued that party politics divided the umma, yet the Brotherhood built its mass base inside professional syndicates: 1, split.
notes.BC: Burke, Thoughts on the Cause of the Present Discontents (1770), defends party as men united on a principle: -1.

Virtue-politics traditions (Confucian, Buddhist, Gandhian, republican-Jacobin, Platonic, Nyerere-style leadership codes, Ho Chi Minh thought) say yes and make it the basis of legitimacy; most others agree mildly; liberal, libertarian, populist and realist camps separate private character from public competence, and Legalism denies that example can govern.

property.2.why: Whether the rise in land value caused by neighbours and infrastructure belongs to the community rather than the landowner (land-value capture). Georgists, left-libertarians, communists, anarchists and land-nationalising socialists say yes by doctrine; social democrats, social liberals and greens favour betterment levies; propertied conservatives, aristocrats and libertarian absolutists defend the owner.

notes.GE: Henry George, Progress and Poverty (1879): rent is created by the community and should be taken by a single land-value tax: 3.
notes.LL: Steiner-Vallentyne left-libertarianism holds that natural resources and land value belong equally to all, with owners paying for the value of the land they hold: 3.
notes.TP: Sun Yat-sen's 'equalisation of land rights' has owners self-assess land value and the state tax and take the future increment: 3.
notes.LZ: The Jewish National Fund holds land as the inalienable property of the Jewish people, leased not sold: 3.
notes.UJ: Nyerere, Ujamaa (1962): land is the gift of God to all, so no one can own it and its value is communal: 3.
notes.UT: J.S. Mill's Land Tenure Reform Association (1870) proposed taking the 'unearned increment' of land value for the public: 2.
notes.PSD: Attlee's Town and Country Planning Act 1947 imposed a 100% development charge on land value increases, following the Uthwatt Report: 2.
notes.CST: Rerum Novarum (1891) defended private land ownership against socialism, and Rome rejected George's remedy in the McGlynn affair (1887): -1.
notes.NEO: Milton Friedman called land value tax 'the least bad tax' and Georgist ideas have economist support, though neoliberals do not give the increment 'to the community': 1, split.
notes.NAZ: Point 17 of the 1920 NSDAP programme demanded abolition of ground rent and land speculation, though it was dropped in practice: 1, split.
notes.ARC: The landed aristocracy's rank and duty rest on inherited estates, so taking land increments undermines it: -3.
notes.AP: The Omaha Platform (1892) says land, with all natural sources of wealth, is the people's heritage and must not be held for speculation: 2.
notes.RS: Vietnam's constitution (Art. 53) and China's land law make land the property of the whole people, managed by the state, which collects land-use revenue: 3.

notes.TR: The 1938 Transitional Programme declares 'the historical crisis of mankind is reduced to the crisis of revolutionary leadership', answered by a vanguard party: 3.
notes.BA: Aflaq and the Ba'ath constitution describe the party as the 'vanguard' (tali'a) of the Arab nation, with a leading role guaranteed in the Syrian and Iraqi constitutions: 3.
notes.RS: Deng's Four Cardinal Principles and Vietnam's Article 4 make the Party the vanguard of the working class and the sole leading force: 3.
notes.CC: Pannekoek and Gorter, 'Open Letter to Comrade Lenin' (1920): the vanguard party leads to party dictatorship; workers must act through their own councils: -3.
notes.AC: Bakunin's quarrel with Marx and Kropotkin's mutual aid reject any enlightened elite ruling the masses: -3.
notes.GAN: Gandhi wanted Congress dissolved into a servants-of-the-people body after independence, refusing a vanguard party of power: -3.
notes.LU: Luxemburg, 'Organisational Questions of Russian Social Democracy' (1904) attacks Lenin's centralism as 'ultra-centralism' that replaces the class with the Central Committee, yet she led the Spartakusbund as a party: -1, split.
notes.TP: Sun Yat-sen's three stages (military rule, tutelage, constitutionalism) put the Kuomintang, as the 'first awakened', in charge until the people are ready: 2.
notes.FA: The Webbs' Soviet Communism: A New Civilisation? (1935) praised the CPSU as a 'vocation of leadership' of trained experts: 1.
notes.TI: The League of Communists of Yugoslavia was a 'leading ideological force' within self-management, not a command party: 2, split.
notes.IF: Fascism's single party was the elite of the nation, not a workers' vanguard: 1, split.

nature.3.why: Whether humanity should engineer the climate (for example stratospheric aerosol injection) if emissions cuts lag. Techno-optimist, technocratic, Soviet-lineage and market-economist camps say yes as a fallback; precautionary greens, Gandhian, Daoist, Christian-humble and traditionalist camps say no.

notes.XC: Xunzi, 'Discourse on Heaven': 'Rather than exalt Heaven and long for it, why not control Heaven's course and use it?': 2.
notes.ML: Soviet climatologist Mikhail Budyko proposed stratospheric sulphur aerosols in 1974, and Soviet planners treated 'transforming nature' as a socialist task: 2.
notes.NEO: Nordhaus and Barrett-style economic analysis treats solar geoengineering as a very cheap insurance option, and David Friedman's 'cheap fix' argues the same: 2.
notes.EM: The Ecomodernist Manifesto (2015) favours technology-led decoupling and calls for research on large-scale options, though not a firm deployment line: 2, split.
notes.TW: Daodejing ch. 29 ('those who would take the world and act on it, I see them fail') makes interference with natural processes the root error: -3.
notes.GAN: Gandhi's Hind Swaraj rejects industrial 'machinery' and its mastery of nature as civilisational disease: -3.
notes.GA: Zerzan and Jensen reject technological fixes as the continuation of domination of nature: -3.
notes.DEG: Degrowth writers (Latouche, Kallis) reject geoengineering as a technological fix that avoids shrinking material throughput: -3.
notes.GM: Green parties generally call for a non-use agreement on solar geoengineering (e.g. 2022 Solar Geoengineering Non-Use Agreement, supported by many greens): -2.
notes.GC: Scruton's Green Philosophy warns against the hubris of planetary management by centralised schemes: -2.
notes.CST: Laudato Si' (2015) criticises the 'technocratic paradigm' and warns against geoengineering fixes that ignore the poor and the causes: -2.
notes.RT: Evola and Guenon treat the project of remaking nature as Promethean pride in the dark age: -3.
notes.NEOR: Land and the accelerationist strand of NRx welcome capital-driven planetary engineering: 2.
